cover: How to read a software quote before you sign

slides.title: A fixed price fixes a number to a scope
slides.body: The developer prices in a margin for the unknown. Anything the scope doesn't name becomes a change request.

slides.title: Time and materials bills the real hours
slides.body: You can change direction without renegotiating. Only your own attention stops the total from growing.

slides.title: Ask who pays when the estimate is wrong
slides.body: Fixed price: the developer, plus the margin you paid up front. Time and materials: you, and you keep any savings.

slides.title: Check what “done” means
slides.body: Look for testing, deployment, handover and support. Some quotes stop at “code delivered” and bill the rest separately.

slides.title: Make sure you own the result
slides.body: Repository, hosting and domain in your name. That decides whether you can take the work elsewhere.

slides.title: Can't describe it yet? Discover first
slides.body: Pay for a short fixed-price discovery, then quote the build once the open questions have answers.
